posts.title: Organic Brown Rice Pea Pilau
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Organic Brown Rice Pea Pilau | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Organic Brown Rice Pea Pilau brings brown rice, peas, tomato, onion, cumin, and warm whole spices into a single covered pot.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.175
posts.body_markdown:
Organic Brown Rice Pea Pilau brings brown rice, peas, tomato, onion, cumin, and warm whole spices into a single covered pot. This pilau is more substantial than a plain rice side but still keeps the seasoning restrained.

Cumin seeds are heated first, followed by onion, tomato, cloves, garlic, and turmeric. The brown rice is stirred into that base before water is added, so the grain begins cooking with the aromatics already distributed through the pot.

The peas are added near the end rather than at the beginning. That timing lets the brown rice cook almost fully before the peas finish the dish, helping them keep more color and texture.

## Ingredients
- 2 teaspoons good oil
- 1 teaspoon whole cumin seeds
- 1 onion, sliced lengthwise, about 1 1/2 cups
- 1 cup tomatoes, chopped
- 2 cloves
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- 1 cup organic short-grain brown rice
- 1/2 teaspoon salt
- 2 1/4 cups water
- 3/4 cup peas

## Method
Heat the oil in a medium pot over medium-high heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds. Reduce the heat to medium, add the onions, and sauté until golden, about 3–4 minutes. Add the tomatoes, cloves, garlic, and turmeric and cook until the tomatoes soften. Stir in the rice and salt, add the water, and bring to a boil. Reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook for 35 minutes. Stir in the peas, cover again, and continue cooking for another 10–15 minutes until the rice is done. Remove the cloves before serving. Makes 3–4 servings.

posts.title: Persian Greens
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Persian Greens combines kidney beans with parsley, spinach, garlic chives, fenugreek leaves, mint, dried lime, and fresh lime juice.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.177
posts.body_markdown:
Persian Greens combines kidney beans with parsley, spinach, garlic chives, fenugreek leaves, mint, dried lime, and fresh lime juice. The result is a bean dish built around a generous quantity of chopped greens and tart citrus notes.

The kidney beans are started separately with onion, turmeric, pepper, and hot water. In another pot, the greens are cooked just until the spinach wilts, then transferred to the beans along with dried limes.

The final simmer brings the beans and greens together before lime juice and salt are added. The source serves the dish with rice and keeps the vegetables and beans clearly distinct rather than puréeing them.

## Ingredients
- 1 1/4 cups dried kidney beans
- 2 tablespoons good oil
- 1 1/2 cups onions, minced
- 1/2 teaspoon turmeric
- Freshly ground pepper to taste
- 1 1/2 cups hot water
- 2 tablespoons good oil
- 1/2 cup fresh parsley, minced
- 1 cup spinach, minced
- 1/4 cup garlic chives, minced
- 1/4 cup fenugreek leaves, minced
- 1 tablespoon fresh mint leaves, minced
- 5 dried limes
- 3–4 tablespoons lime juice, or to taste
- Salt to taste

## Method
Soak the kidney beans overnight or for at least 1 hour, then drain. Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a pot over medium heat and sauté the onions until golden, about 6 minutes. Add turmeric and cook for 1 minute, then add the beans, pepper, and hot water. Cover and simmer gently until the beans are about half cooked. In a separate pot, heat the remaining oil and cook the parsley, spinach, garlic chives, and fenugreek leaves until the spinach wilts, about 3–4 minutes. Add the greens to the beans with the dried limes, cover, reduce the heat to medium-low, and simmer for 30 minutes. Add the lime juice and salt and cook for another 5–10 minutes. Makes 4 servings.

posts.title: Spinach & Broccoli Baji
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Spinach & Broccoli Baji is a soft, puréed vegetable dish built around slowly caramelized onions.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.179
posts.body_markdown:
Spinach & Broccoli Baji is a soft, puréed vegetable dish built around slowly caramelized onions. The source treats that first step as the key to balancing the strong flavor of the greens.

Butter or ghee and olive oil form the cooking base, followed by onion, ginger, and optional green chili. Spinach and broccoli are then covered and cooked gently with salt until fully softened.

The vegetables are puréed only after they have cooked through. The finished baji is smooth enough to serve alongside chapatis or rice while still tasting clearly of spinach and broccoli.

## Ingredients
- 1 teaspoon butter or ghee
- 2 teaspoons olive oil
- 1 large or 2 small onions, sliced, about 1 1/2 cups
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1 fresh green chili, slit at the end, optional
- 5–6 cups spinach, chopped
- 1 head broccoli, roughly chopped
- 1 teaspoon salt, or to taste

## Method
Heat the butter or ghee and olive oil in a large pot over medium-low heat. Add the onions, ginger, and optional green chili and sauté until the onions are well caramelized, about 8 minutes. Add the spinach, broccoli, and salt, cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 20–30 minutes until the vegetables are very soft. Remove from the heat and carefully purée in a blender or food processor until smooth. Makes 4 servings.

posts.title: Palak Paneer
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Palak Paneer is presented in the source as a direct variation on Spinach & Broccoli Baji.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.180
posts.body_markdown:
Palak Paneer is presented in the source as a direct variation on Spinach & Broccoli Baji. The smooth green vegetable base is prepared first, then cubes of paneer are folded through at the end.

Because the paneer is not browned separately in this version, its soft texture remains distinct from the puréed spinach and broccoli. The contrast is simple and central to the dish.

The source also suggests goat’s feta or goat’s cheese as an alternative variation. The base method below follows the paneer version and keeps the seasoning identical to the preceding baji recipe.

## Ingredients
- 1 teaspoon butter or ghee
- 2 teaspoons olive oil
- 1 large or 2 small onions, sliced, about 1 1/2 cups
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1 fresh green chili, slit at the end, optional
- 5–6 cups spinach, chopped
- 1 head broccoli, roughly chopped
- 1 teaspoon salt, or to taste
- 1 cup paneer, cut into 1-inch cubes

## Method
Prepare the Spinach & Broccoli Baji base by heating the butter or ghee and olive oil over medium-low heat. Add the onions, ginger, and optional chili and cook until the onions caramelize, about 8 minutes. Add the spinach, broccoli, and salt, cover, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 20–30 minutes. Purée the cooked vegetables carefully until smooth. Return the mixture to the pot if needed, add the paneer cubes, toss gently until evenly coated and warmed through, and serve. Makes about 4–5 servings.

posts.title: African Spinach
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: African Spinach is a very short stovetop recipe in which spinach cooks with ghee, olive oil, garlic, and vegetable bouillon.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.181
posts.body_markdown:
African Spinach is a very short stovetop recipe in which spinach cooks with ghee, olive oil, garlic, and vegetable bouillon. The simplicity keeps the greens at the center of the dish.

Garlic is sautéed only briefly before the spinach is added. The pan is then covered so the packed leaves wilt in their own moisture with the bouillon seasoning.

Salt is adjusted only after cooking. The source also notes that chopped kale can be substituted for spinach if a sturdier green is preferred.

## Ingredients
- 1 teaspoon ghee
- 1 teaspoon olive oil
- 1–2 teaspoons garlic, crushed
- 6 cups spinach, packed
- 2 teaspoons vegetable bouillon powder
- Salt to taste

## Method
Melt the ghee with the olive oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the garlic and sauté for about 30 seconds without letting it brown deeply. Add the spinach and vegetable bouillon, cover the pot, and cook for 8–10 minutes until the spinach is fully wilted and tender. Taste, add salt if needed, and serve warm. For the source variation, substitute chopped kale for the spinach and cook until tender. Makes 2 servings.

posts.title: Steamed Swiss Chard with Balsamic Vinegar
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Steamed Swiss Chard with Balsamic Vinegar | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Steamed Swiss Chard with Balsamic Vinegar uses a quick covered-pan method rather than boiling the greens.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.182
posts.body_markdown:
Steamed Swiss Chard with Balsamic Vinegar uses a quick covered-pan method rather than boiling the greens. The chard is tossed with a small amount of oil, salt, and pepper before steaming.

A first short steam begins the wilting process, then the chard is tossed and covered again until tender. This keeps the cooking time brief and avoids saturating the leaves with water.

Additional olive oil and balsamic vinegar are added only after the pan comes off the heat. The warm greens absorb the dressing while still keeping the balsamic flavor distinct.

## Ingredients
- 2 teaspoons olive oil
- 5 cups packed Swiss chard leaves, chopped
- Salt to taste
- Freshly ground pepper to taste
- 1–2 tablespoons olive oil, for tossing
- 1–2 tablespoons balsamic vinegar

## Method
Heat 2 teaspoons olive oil in a large pot or frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the Swiss chard, salt, and pepper and toss to coat. Cover and steam for 1–2 minutes. Toss again, cover, and steam for another 3–4 minutes, until the leaves are tender. Remove from the heat and toss with the additional olive oil and balsamic vinegar to taste. Serve while still warm.

posts.title: Mama’s Mushroom & Spinach Pie
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Mama’s Mushroom & Spinach Pie wraps a cooked spinach-and-mushroom filling in pastry, then bakes the filled log until golden.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.183
posts.body_markdown:
Mama’s Mushroom & Spinach Pie wraps a cooked spinach-and-mushroom filling in pastry, then bakes the filled log until golden. It works as either a lunch or dinner dish and pairs naturally with a simple salad.

Mushrooms, green onions, ginger, garlic, and green chili are sautéed before spinach is added. The vegetable mixture is cooled before it is combined with beaten egg and grated mozzarella.

The pastry is rolled into a rectangle, filled, sealed, glazed with egg white, and baked seam-side down. The source allows either frozen chopped spinach or an equivalent quantity of fresh spinach that has been wilted and squeezed dry.

## Ingredients
- 2 teaspoons good oil
- 1 cup mushrooms, sliced and quartered
- 1/2 cup green onions, sliced
- 1/2 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1/2 teaspoon garlic, minced
- 1/2 teaspoon fresh green chilies, minced
- Salt to taste
- Freshly ground pepper to taste
- 10 ounces frozen chopped spinach, thawed and squeezed dry
- 1 egg
- 1 cup mozzarella cheese, grated
- Pastry shell or filo pastry
- 1 egg white, for glazing

## Method
Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and sauté the mushrooms, green onions, ginger, garlic, and chili until the mushrooms soften. Season with salt and pepper, add the spinach, and cook about 3 minutes. Remove from the heat and cool. Beat the egg in a large bowl, mix in the mozzarella, then fold in the cooled spinach mixture. Roll the pastry into a rectangle about 12 by 18 inches, place the filling in the center, and fold into a sealed log. Place seam-side down on an oiled baking sheet, brush with egg white, and bake for 45 minutes. Slice into 2-inch pieces. Makes 3–4 servings.

posts.title: Eat Your Curried Green Peas
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Eat Your Curried Green Peas | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Eat Your Curried Green Peas turns fresh peas into a complete curry with onion, tomato, ginger, garlic, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and garam masala.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.184
posts.body_markdown:
Eat Your Curried Green Peas turns fresh peas into a complete curry with onion, tomato, ginger, garlic, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and garam masala. The peas remain the main ingredient rather than a garnish.

The sauce is built first by cooking the aromatics and dry spices, then softening the tomatoes and tomato purée. Only after that base is ready are the peas and water added.

Lemon juice is stirred in at the end, followed by garam masala and cilantro. The source also gives a paneer variation, but the base recipe below keeps the dish focused on the peas.

## Ingredients
- 1 tablespoon good oil
- 1/2 cup onions, minced
- 1 teaspoon garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 teaspoon ground coriander
- 1/2 teaspoon turmeric
- 1/4–1 teaspoon cayenne pepper
- 2 cups tomatoes, diced with their juices
- 1 tablespoon tomato purée
- 1 1/4 teaspoons salt, or to taste
- 1 1/2 tablespoons fresh cilantro leaves, chopped
- 4 cups fresh green peas
- 1 cup water
- Juice of 1/2 lemon
- 1/2 teaspoon garam masala
- 1 1/2 tablespoons fresh cilantro leaves, chopped, for garnish

## Method
Heat the oil in a pot over high heat. Add the onions, garlic, and ginger, reduce to medium, and sauté until the onions are golden, about 3–5 minutes. Add the cumin, coriander, turmeric, and cayenne and cook for 30 seconds. Add the tomatoes, tomato purée, salt, and 1 1/2 tablespoons cilantro and cook about 5 minutes until the tomatoes soften. Stir in the peas and water, bring to a boil, cover, reduce the heat, and simmer about 10 minutes until the peas are done. Adjust the salt, stir in the lemon juice, then finish with garam masala and the remaining cilantro. Makes 4 servings.

posts.title: Fresh Green Pea & Potato Curry
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Fresh Green Pea & Potato Curry | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Fresh Green Pea & Potato Curry combines boiled potato and fresh peas with a tomato-based masala.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.185
posts.body_markdown:
Fresh Green Pea & Potato Curry combines boiled potato and fresh peas with a tomato-based masala. The potatoes start cooking in the sauce before the peas are added, giving the two vegetables different textures.

Cumin seeds are heated first, followed by onion, ginger, and garlic. Tomato, tomato purée, turmeric, cumin, coriander, garam masala, and cayenne form the seasoned base.

Water is added with the peas only after the potatoes have begun to soften. Lemon juice and cilantro finish the curry once the peas are tender.

## Ingredients
- 2 teaspoons good oil
- 1 teaspoon whole cumin seeds
- 1/2 cup onions, chopped
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1 clove garlic, minced
- 1 cup tomatoes, diced
- 2 teaspoons tomato purée
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- 1/2 teaspoon salt, or to taste
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 teaspoon ground coriander
- 1/2 teaspoon garam masala
- 1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper, or 1 teaspoon chopped green chili
- 2 cups potatoes, cubed
- 2 cups fresh green peas
- 1 cup water
- Juice of 1/2 lemon
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped

## Method
Heat the oil in a pot over medium-high heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds. Add the onions, ginger, and garlic, reduce to medium, and sauté until the onions are golden, about 4–6 minutes. Add the tomatoes, tomato purée, turmeric, salt, ground cumin, coriander, garam masala, and cayenne and cook for 3–4 minutes. Add the potatoes and cook until they begin to soften. Add the peas and water, bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer, and cook about 10 minutes until the peas are done. Stir in the lemon juice, adjust the salt, garnish with cilantro, and serve. Makes 2–4 servings.

posts.title: Pea & Mushroom Curry
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Pea & Mushroom Curry is a compact stovetop dish with a yogurt-based sauce.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.186
posts.body_markdown:
Pea & Mushroom Curry is a compact stovetop dish with a yogurt-based sauce. Mustard seeds, caramelized onion, turmeric, and garam masala provide most of the seasoning.

The yogurt is brought to a boil with the spices before the peas are added. Mushrooms join a few minutes later, allowing the peas to begin cooking first.

The pan stays covered during the final simmer so the mushrooms soften and release moisture into the sauce. The source keeps the ingredient list short and finishes simply by adjusting the salt.

## Ingredients
- 1 tablespoon good oil
- 1/2 teaspoon black mustard seeds
- 3/4 cup onions, minced
- 1/2 teaspoon turmeric
- 1 teaspoon garam masala
- 1/3 cup plain yogurt
- 1 teaspoon salt, or to taste
- 3 cups fresh green peas
- 3 cups mushrooms, sliced

## Method
Heat the oil in a pot over medium-high heat. Add the mustard seeds, cover, and let them pop for 30 seconds. Add the onions, reduce the heat to medium-low, and sauté until golden, about 6–8 minutes. Stir in the turmeric and garam masala for about 30 seconds. Add the yogurt and salt, increase the heat to medium-high, and bring to a boil. Reduce to medium, add the peas, and cook for 3 minutes. Add the mushrooms, cover, and continue cooking for 10–15 minutes until the peas and mushrooms are tender. Adjust the salt and serve. Makes 4 servings.

posts.title: Alu Methi
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Alu Methi pairs cooked potatoes with fresh fenugreek leaves in a tomato, onion, ginger, and cumin base.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.187
posts.body_markdown:
Alu Methi pairs cooked potatoes with fresh fenugreek leaves in a tomato, onion, ginger, and cumin base. The fenugreek gives the dish its distinct bitter edge.

Cumin seeds are heated first, followed by onion. Green chili, ginger, turmeric, salt, and tomato are then cooked until the tomato softens and the seasoning becomes cohesive.

The potatoes and fenugreek go in last. The leaves wilt quickly, so the final cooking stage is short and the potatoes remain clearly defined rather than breaking down into a sauce.

## Ingredients
- 1 tablespoon good oil
- 1/2 teaspoon whole cumin seeds
- 1 cup onions, minced
- 1–2 fresh green chilies, minced
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1/2 teaspoon turmeric
- Salt to taste
- 1 cup tomatoes, diced
- 4 cups potatoes, boiled, peeled, and diced
- 1 cup fenugreek leaves, chopped

## Method
Heat the oil in a pot over medium-high heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds. Add the onions and sauté until just golden, about 3–4 minutes. Add the chilies, ginger, turmeric, salt, and tomatoes. Reduce the heat to medium and cook until the tomatoes soften, about 5–7 minutes. Add the potatoes and fenugreek leaves and cook until the fenugreek wilts, about 5 minutes. Stir well and serve. Makes 4 servings.

posts.title: Lata’s Green Masala with Paneer
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Lata’s Green Masala with Paneer | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Lata’s Green Masala with Paneer is a rich paneer dish built around slow-cooked onion, green chili, ginger, garlic, whole spices, cilantro, and sour cream.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.188
posts.body_markdown:
Lata’s Green Masala with Paneer is a rich paneer dish built around slow-cooked onion, green chili, ginger, garlic, whole spices, cilantro, and sour cream.

The onion mixture and paneer are prepared in separate pans. Mustard seeds and turmeric season the paneer before it is folded into the caramelized onion and whole-spice masala.

Sour cream is tempered with a small spoonful of the hot mixture before being stirred into the pan, a step the source uses to reduce the risk of curdling. Whole spices are removed before serving.

## Ingredients
- 2 tablespoons ghee, or 1 tablespoon ghee or butter plus 1 tablespoon light oil
- 1 1/2 cups onions, minced
- 2 tablespoons fresh green chilies, chopped
- 5 tablespoons fresh ginger, minced
- 3 teaspoons garlic, minced
- 12 whole peppercorns
- 4 bay leaves
- 5 cloves
- 2 teaspoons olive oil or ghee
- 1 1/2 teaspoons black mustard seeds
- 1/2 teaspoon turmeric
- 3 cups paneer, cut into 3/4-inch cubes
- 2 cups fresh cilantro leaves, packed and roughly chopped
- 1 cup sour cream

## Method
Melt the ghee in a large frying pan over medium-low heat. Add the onions and sauté until caramelized, about 8–10 minutes. Add the chilies, ginger, garlic, peppercorns, bay leaves, and cloves. In a second small frying pan, heat the olive oil or ghee over medium-high heat, add the mustard seeds, cover, and let them pop for 30 seconds. Reduce to medium, stir in the turmeric for 30 seconds, then add the paneer and sauté for 1 minute. Transfer the paneer to the onion mixture, remove from the heat, add the cilantro, and mix. Remove the peppercorns, bay leaves, and cloves. Stir 2 tablespoons of the hot mixture into the sour cream, then fold that tempered sour cream back into the pan. Serve with rice.

posts.title: Fit for a King Eggplant Bharta
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Fit for a King Eggplant Bharta | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Fit for a King Eggplant Bharta relies on thoroughly broiling whole eggplants until they collapse.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.189
posts.body_markdown:
Fit for a King Eggplant Bharta relies on thoroughly broiling whole eggplants until they collapse. That deep softening gives the mashed pulp the texture needed for the finished bharta.

After cooling, the flesh is removed from the skins and mashed. Cumin seeds, onion, ginger, tomato, salt, and green chili are cooked separately until the onions and tomatoes are fully softened.

The mashed eggplant is then added back to the pan and cooked slowly until it begins to catch slightly on the bottom. Cilantro is used only at the end.

## Ingredients
- 2 large eggplants
- A little olive oil, for coating
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 1/2 teaspoons whole cumin seeds
- 2 medium onions, chopped
- 1 1/2 teaspoons fresh ginger, minced
- 3 medium tomatoes, diced
- 1 teaspoon salt, or to taste
- 1–2 teaspoons fresh green chilies, minced
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped

## Method
Set the oven to broil. Wash and dry the eggplants, pierce both ends with a fork, rub lightly with olive oil, and broil for about 20 minutes per side until completely soft and collapsed. Cool fully, scoop out the flesh, and chop or mash it. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds. Add the onions, reduce to medium, and sauté until golden, about 5–7 minutes. Add the ginger, tomatoes, salt, and chilies and cook until the tomatoes soften, about 4–5 minutes. Add the eggplant, reduce to medium-low, and cook another 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. Garnish with cilantro. Makes 2–4 servings.

posts.title: Indian Fusion Ratatouille
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Indian Fusion Ratatouille combines eggplant, shing qua, chayote, tomato, and Indian spices in a slow vegetable braise.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.190
posts.body_markdown:
Indian Fusion Ratatouille combines eggplant, shing qua, chayote, tomato, and Indian spices in a slow vegetable braise. The source presents it as a meeting point between market vegetables and familiar Indian seasoning.

Onion, ginger, garlic, and green chili are sautéed first, followed by cilantro, turmeric, cayenne, cumin, coriander, and salt. The remaining vegetables then cook together under a lid.

The dish begins with a short medium-heat stage and finishes with a longer, gentler simmer. That gives the vegetables time to soften and absorb the seasoning without being puréed.

## Ingredients
- 2 tablespoons olive oil
- 3/4 cup onions, minced
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 2 cloves garlic, minced
- 1 fresh green chili, minced
- 1/2 cup fresh cilantro leaves or parsley, chopped
- 1/2 teaspoon turmeric
- 1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 teaspoon ground coriander
- Salt to taste
- 3 tomatoes, cubed
- 1 long Japanese eggplant, sliced
- 1 small round eggplant, cubed
- 1 shing qua, cubed
- 1 chayote, thinly sliced

## Method
Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the onions, ginger, garlic, and chili and sauté until the onions are golden, about 3–4 minutes. Add the cilantro, turmeric, cayenne, cumin, coriander, and salt and stir well. Add the tomatoes, both eggplants, shing qua, and chayote. Cover, reduce the heat to medium, and cook for 6–8 minutes. Stir, cover again, reduce to medium-low, and simmer for 30–40 minutes until the vegetables are very tender. Adjust the seasoning and serve over rice. Makes 2–4 servings.

posts.title: Soft & Spicy Eggplant Curry
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Soft & Spicy Eggplant Curry combines cubed eggplant with peas in a mustard-seed and tomato base.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.191
posts.body_markdown:
Soft & Spicy Eggplant Curry combines cubed eggplant with peas in a mustard-seed and tomato base. The vegetables are cooked under a lid so the eggplant softens into the sauce.

Mustard seeds are popped first, then onion, salt, turmeric, cayenne, and optional hing are sautéed until the onion turns golden. Tomato and eggplant go in before the peas.

A small amount of water is added only after the eggplant has already cooked for several minutes. Cilantro finishes the dish without changing the soft texture of the curry.

## Ingredients
- 1 tablespoon good oil
- 1 1/2 teaspoons black mustard seeds
- 1 1/2 cups onions, chopped
- 1 teaspoon salt, or to taste
- 1/2 teaspoon turmeric
- 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper, or to taste
- 1/8 teaspoon hing, optional
- 1 cup tomatoes, chopped
- 6 cups eggplant, cubed
- 1 1/2 cups fresh green peas
- 3/4 cup water
- 1 tablespoon fresh cilantro leaves, chopped

## Method
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the mustard seeds, cover, and let them pop for 30 seconds. Add the onions, salt, turmeric, cayenne, and optional hing and sauté until the onions are golden, about 4–5 minutes. Add the tomatoes and eggplant, mix well, cover, and cook for 10 minutes. Add the peas and water and continue cooking for about 5 minutes, or until the peas are tender. Check the seasoning, garnish with cilantro, and serve. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: Meena’s Zucchini & Squash Medley
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Meena’s Zucchini & Squash Medley is a quick sauté that keeps the seasoning minimal.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.192
posts.body_markdown:
Meena’s Zucchini & Squash Medley is a quick sauté that keeps the seasoning minimal. Zucchini and squash are the focus, with coriander, lime, and cilantro adding only a light frame.

The vegetables are first tossed over medium-high heat so they begin to soften and take on a little color. Ground coriander is added only after the first few minutes.

The pan is then covered briefly to finish the vegetables. Salt and lime juice are stirred in at the end, and cilantro is used as a fresh garnish.

## Ingredients
- 1–2 tablespoons olive oil
- 2 cups zucchini, diced
- 2 cups squash, diced
- 1 teaspoon ground coriander
- Salt to taste
- Juice of 1/2 lime
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped

## Method
Heat the olive oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the zucchini and squash and sauté for 4–5 minutes, tossing regularly. Reduce the heat to medium, add the coriander, stir, cover, and cook for another 5–7 minutes until the vegetables are soft. Add salt and lime juice, toss gently, garnish with cilantro, and serve. Makes 2–4 servings.

posts.title: Broccoli, Cauliflower & Potato Baji
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Broccoli, Cauliflower & Potato Baji cooks three sturdy vegetables together with onion, ginger, turmeric, chili, and garam masala.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.193
posts.body_markdown:
Broccoli, Cauliflower & Potato Baji cooks three sturdy vegetables together with onion, ginger, turmeric, chili, and garam masala. The source adapts a traditional cauliflower preparation by adding broccoli.

The aromatics are sautéed only briefly before the potatoes, broccoli, and cauliflower are added. The pan is then covered so the vegetables soften mostly in their own moisture.

Garam masala and pepper are added near the end, with cilantro as the final garnish. The source suggests adding only a small amount of water if the vegetables truly need it.

## Ingredients
- 2 teaspoons good oil
- 3/4–1 cup onions, quartered
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- 1 fresh green chili, slit at the end or minced
- 1 cup potatoes, thinly sliced
- 2 cups broccoli florets
- 2 cups cauliflower florets
- Salt to taste
- 1/2 teaspoon garam masala
- Freshly ground pepper to taste
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped

## Method
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the onions, ginger, turmeric, and chili and sauté for 2–3 minutes until the onions begin to soften. Add the potatoes, broccoli, cauliflower, and salt and mix well. Cover and cook until the vegetables are soft, about 15 minutes, adding up to 1/4 cup water only if needed. Continue until fully done, then sprinkle with garam masala and pepper. Remove the whole chili if used, garnish with cilantro, and serve. Makes 4–5 servings.

posts.title: Delectable Curried Cauliflower with Ginger & Tomatoes
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Delectable Curried Cauliflower with Ginger & Tomatoes | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Delectable Curried Cauliflower with Ginger & Tomatoes is a one-pan cauliflower dish with cumin, ginger, turmeric, cayenne, tomato, and garam masala.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.194
posts.body_markdown:
Delectable Curried Cauliflower with Ginger & Tomatoes is a one-pan cauliflower dish with cumin, ginger, turmeric, cayenne, tomato, and garam masala.

The cumin seeds are heated first, followed by ginger, turmeric, cayenne, and tomatoes. This lets the spice base cook before the cauliflower goes in.

The cauliflower then cooks covered until tender. Garam masala appears both during cooking and as a final garnish, while fresh cilantro is added only at the end.

## Ingredients
- 1 tablespoon good oil
- 1 teaspoon whole cumin seeds
- 1 tablespoon fresh ginger, minced
- 3/4 teaspoon turmeric
- 1/2–1 teaspoon cayenne pepper
- 3 cups tomatoes, chopped
- 1 large head cauliflower, cut into florets
- Salt to taste
- 3/4 teaspoon garam masala
- 1/4 teaspoon garam masala, for garnish
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped

## Method
Heat the oil in a pot over medium-high heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds. Add the ginger, turmeric, cayenne, and tomatoes and sauté for 3–4 minutes. Add the cauliflower, salt, and 3/4 teaspoon garam masala. Stir, cover, and cook for 10–15 minutes until the cauliflower is tender. Sprinkle with the remaining garam masala, garnish with cilantro, and serve. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: French Bean & Tomato Cumin Sauté
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: French Bean & Tomato Cumin Sauté | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: French Bean & Tomato Cumin Sauté is a fast skillet dish with French green beans, tomato, onion, cumin, turmeric, and cayenne.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.195
posts.body_markdown:
French Bean & Tomato Cumin Sauté is a fast skillet dish with French green beans, tomato, onion, cumin, turmeric, and cayenne. The beans are cooked just until tender rather than simmered for a long time.

Cumin seeds are heated first, then onion is sautéed briefly before tomato and beans are added with the remaining spices. The covered pan traps enough steam to finish the vegetables.

The source allows a small amount of water if the pan becomes too dry. Otherwise the tomatoes provide most of the moisture for this short cooking method.

## Ingredients
- 2 teaspoons coconut oil or other good oil
- 1 1/2 teaspoons whole cumin seeds
- 1/3 cup onions, chopped
- 1/2 cup tomatoes, chopped
- 1 1/2 cups long French green beans
- 1/2 teaspoon turmeric
- 1/4–1 teaspoon cayenne pepper
- Salt to taste

## Method
Heat the oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds. Add the onions and sauté for 1–2 minutes. Reduce the heat to medium, then add the tomatoes, beans, turmeric, cayenne, and salt. Stir, cover, and cook for 5–10 minutes until the beans are tender. If the pan needs more liquid, add up to 1/4 cup water. Makes 2 servings.

posts.title: Basia’s No Fuss French Green Beans
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.seo_title: Basia’s No Fuss French Green Beans | WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Basia’s No Fuss French Green Beans keeps the beans crisp by blanching them briefly and immediately cooling them in iced water.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.196
posts.body_markdown:
Basia’s No Fuss French Green Beans keeps the beans crisp by blanching them briefly and immediately cooling them in iced water. The dressing and toppings are added only after that cooking is stopped.

Red bell pepper, red onion, and crumbled goat’s cheese bring color and texture, while olive oil, balsamic vinegar, lemon, and mustard create a sharp dressing.

Because the beans are not returned to heat, the final dish stays bright and fresh. The source also offers a variation with sautéed onion for a softer flavor.

## Ingredients
- 5 cups French green beans
- 6 cups iced water
- 1 cup red bell peppers, finely diced
- 1/2 cup red onions, finely diced
- 1/2 cup goat’s cheese, crumbled
- 4–5 tablespoons olive oil
- 3 tablespoons balsamic vinegar
- Juice of 1/2 lemon
- 1/4 teaspoon dry mustard, or 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard
- Salt to taste
- Freshly ground pepper to taste

## Method
Bring a large pot of water to a boil, add the beans, reduce the heat to medium-high, and blanch for 3–5 minutes until tender and bright green. Transfer immediately to iced water to stop the cooking, then drain well. Place the beans in a serving bowl and add the bell pepper, red onion, goat’s cheese, olive oil, balsamic vinegar, lemon juice, mustard, salt, and pepper. Toss thoroughly, check the seasoning, and serve. Makes 6–8 servings.

posts.title: Traditional Vegetable Curry
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Traditional Vegetable Curry is a classic mixed-vegetable curry built from caramelized onion, tomato, tomato paste, garlic, ginger, chili, and several whole spices.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.197
posts.body_markdown:
Traditional Vegetable Curry is a classic mixed-vegetable curry built from caramelized onion, tomato, tomato paste, garlic, ginger, chili, and several whole and ground spices.

The sauce is developed before the vegetables are added. Cinnamon, cardamom, peppercorns, turmeric, cayenne, coriander, and cumin all cook with the tomato base until the tomatoes soften.

Mixed vegetables then simmer under a lid with water. Lemon, garam masala, and cilantro are added at the end, and the whole spices can be removed before serving.

## Ingredients
- 2 teaspoons good oil
- 1 cup onions, minced
- 1 teaspoon garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 1/2–1 1/2 teaspoons fresh green chilies, minced
- 1 1/2 cups tomatoes, chopped with their juices
- 2 tablespoons tomato paste
- 1 cinnamon stick, about 2 inches long
- 2 cardamom pods, slit at the end
- 4 whole black peppercorns
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- 1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper
- 1 teaspoon ground coriander
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 teaspoon salt, or to taste
- 6 cups mixed vegetables
- 1 cup water
- Juice of 1/2 lemon
- 1/2–1 teaspoon garam masala
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped

## Method
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-low heat. Add the onions and sauté until soft, about 3–4 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, and chilies and continue for 4–5 minutes until the onions are caramelized. Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, cinnamon, cardamom, peppercorns, turmeric, cayenne, coriander, cumin, and salt. Increase to medium and cook for 5–10 minutes until the tomatoes soften. Add the mixed vegetables and water, cover, and cook for 25 minutes, adding small amounts of water if needed. Stir in the lemon juice, sprinkle with garam masala and cilantro, and remove the whole spices before serving if preferred. Makes 4–6 servings.

posts.title: Karela
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Karela is a bitter-gourd and potato dish that takes more preparation than most recipes in the section.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.199
posts.body_markdown:
Karela is a bitter-gourd and potato dish that takes more preparation than most recipes in the section. The gourd is first salted and pressed for several hours before being rinsed and squeezed dry.

The bitter gourd and potatoes are fried separately until crisp. Onion is then cooked in the same pan before tomato, tomato paste, garlic, ginger, chili, spices, and hing form the masala.

The vegetables return to the pan for a final sauté. Gur and lemon juice balance the bitter flavor, while garam masala and cilantro are added just before serving.

## Ingredients
- 4 cups bitter gourd, peeled and sliced into 1/4-inch rounds
- 2 teaspoons salt, for sweating
- 1/2 cup good oil
- 4 cups potatoes, peeled and sliced
- 1 cup onions, thinly sliced
- 2 cups tomatoes, diced
- 2 teaspoons tomato paste
- 1 teaspoon garlic, minced
- 1 teaspoon fresh ginger, minced
- 2 teaspoons fresh green chilies, minced
- 1 teaspoon ground cumin
- 1 teaspoon ground coriander
- 1 teaspoon garam masala
- 1/4 teaspoon turmeric
- Pinch of hing
- 1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper
- Salt to taste
- 2 teaspoons gur or brown sugar
- Juice of 1/2 lemon
- 1/2 teaspoon garam masala, for garnish
- 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, chopped

## Method
Place the sliced bitter gourd in a large bowl, sprinkle with salt, set a plate and heavy can on top, and leave it to sweat for 4 hours. Rinse thoroughly and squeeze out the excess liquid. Heat the oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat and fry the bitter gourd on both sides for 3–4 minutes until crisp; remove and set aside. Fry the potatoes until crisp and set them aside. Reduce the heat to medium and sauté the onions until golden, about 5–7 minutes; remove half. Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, garlic, ginger, chilies, cumin, coriander, garam masala, turmeric, hing, cayenne, and salt and cook about 7 minutes. Return the gourd, potatoes, and reserved onions and sauté another 5 minutes. Stir in the gur until dissolved, add lemon juice, then finish with garam masala and cilantro. Makes 6–8 servings.

posts.title: Matteo’s Simply Delicious Asparagus
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Matteo’s Simply Delicious Asparagus uses a two-stage method: a short boil to soften the spears, followed by a brief broil with ghee and Parmesan.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.200
posts.body_markdown:
Matteo’s Simply Delicious Asparagus uses a two-stage method: a short boil to soften the spears, followed by a brief broil with ghee and Parmesan.

The asparagus is intentionally kept slightly crisp after boiling. That prevents it from becoming too soft during the final oven stage.

Ghee, Parmesan, salt, and pepper provide all of the seasoning. The broiler is used only until the cheese begins to brown, so the dish comes together quickly.

## Ingredients
- 1 bunch thin asparagus
- 1 tablespoon ghee or butter
- 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese, grated
- Salt to taste
- Freshly ground pepper to taste

## Method
Set the oven to broil. Bring a large pot of water to a boil, add the asparagus, reduce the heat to medium-high, and cook for 4–5 minutes until the spears begin to soften but remain crisp. Drain and transfer the asparagus to a baking dish. Dot with ghee or butter, sprinkle with Parmesan, salt, and pepper, and broil for 2–3 minutes until the cheese begins to brown. Serve immediately. Makes 4 servings.

posts.title: Malu’s Bhindi
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Malu’s Bhindi is a quick okra preparation seasoned with mustard seeds, cumin seeds, hing, turmeric, cayenne, and salt.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.201
posts.body_markdown:
Malu’s Bhindi is a quick okra preparation seasoned with mustard seeds, cumin seeds, hing, turmeric, cayenne, and salt. The dish is cooked entirely in one frying pan.

Mustard seeds are popped first, followed by cumin and hing. The sliced okra is then coated in that spice-infused oil before the ground spices are added.

The okra cooks over medium heat until softened. The source allows a small amount of water if needed, but the basic preparation is relatively dry rather than saucy.

## Ingredients
- 1 tablespoon good oil
- 1/2 teaspoon mustard seeds
- 1 teaspoon whole cumin seeds
- 1/8 teaspoon hing, optional
- 4 cups okra, sliced into 1-inch pieces
- 1/2 teaspoon turmeric
- 1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper
- Salt to taste

## Method
Heat the oil in a heavy-bottomed or non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the mustard seeds, cover, and let them pop for 30 seconds. Add the cumin seeds and optional hing and let them sizzle for 20 seconds. Add the okra and mix well. Reduce the heat to medium, add the turmeric, cayenne, and salt, and cook for about 10 minutes until the okra is tender. If the pan becomes too dry, add up to 1/4 cup water. Makes 4 servings.

posts.title: Squash Heaven
posts.author: Anew by WECARE.DIGITAL
posts.meta_description: Squash Heaven fills roasted winter squash with a savory brown-rice mixture.
posts.source_ref: The Modern Ayurvedic Cookbook, book p.202
posts.body_markdown:
Squash Heaven fills roasted winter squash with a savory brown-rice mixture. The soft, lightly sweet squash contrasts with feta, toasted nuts or seeds, herbs, and pepper.

The squash is roasted cut-side down until tender, then brushed with maple syrup. The rice is cooked separately with vegetable bouillon before being combined with the remaining filling ingredients.

Once the squash is soft, the rice mixture is spooned directly into the cavity. There is no second baking stage in the source; the hot squash and prepared filling are simply assembled and served.

## Ingredients
- 1 1/2 cups cooked brown rice, prepared with 1 teaspoon vegetable bouillon powder
- 1 large butternut squash, acorn squash, or other winter squash
- 1 teaspoon maple syrup
- 1/2 cup feta cheese, crumbled
- 1/4 cup walnuts or sunflower seeds, toasted
- 1 teaspoon gomasio
- 1/2 cup fresh parsley, chopped
- 1/4 cup fresh herbs, chopped, such as oregano, chives, or basil
- Freshly ground pepper to taste

## Method
Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C). Cut the squash in half, scoop out and discard the seeds, and place the halves cut-side down on a baking sheet. Bake for 45–60 minutes, depending on size, until tender when pierced with a fork. Remove from the oven and coat the cut surfaces with maple syrup. In a medium bowl, toss the cooked brown rice with the feta, toasted walnuts or sunflower seeds, gomasio, parsley, fresh herbs, and pepper. Fill the roasted squash halves with the rice mixture and serve. Makes 2 servings.
